discussion_comments.comment_body:
Partly fixed in bcacaa03, partly disagreeing.

Fixed: `scanned_child_pids` now streams `/proc` (`proc_pids()`) instead of materializing every pid, and stops one past `CHILD_GROUPS_SCAN_LIMIT` — one past is all the caller needs to return `None`, so the child-group fallback fails closed without reading the rest of the process table. Split out `scanned_child_pids_from` so the bound and the ppid filter are unit tested.

Not changing: the member-discovery sweep in `foreground_process_group_members_with` stays uncapped on purpose. Membership is decided by pgid, and `/proc` has no pgid -> pid index, so finding a group's members is inherently a full sweep — `session_processes()` in this same file already does exactly that for session ids. A cap there would truncate by readdir order, which is where the process this PR is about tends to land (the agent is spawned after its wrapper, so it has the higher pid), and would silently reintroduce the bug on busy hosts. The sweep only runs at all when the kernel probe reports no children files, and only when `should_probe_foreground_job` lets a probe through.

On materializing pids in that path specifically: the cost is the readdir plus one `/proc/<pid>/stat` read per pid, and streaming does not avoid either since every candidate must be inspected anyway. The `Vec` itself is a few thousand `u32`s, and it is the seam that keeps these functions injectable in tests, so I would rather keep it.

Fixed in 38ed0851. The walk now keeps one breadth-first frontier per root and advances them round-robin, so the shared 512-node budget is spent across the foreground-group leader's subtree and the pane shell's descendants instead of one exhausting it. The shell root and its children are reached even when the leader subtree exceeds the bound, and the leader subtree is reached when the shell backlog exceeds it.

Added a second regression test,  oreground_tree_traversal_shares_the_scan_limit_between_roots, where the leader has 700+ descendants and a shell-side foreground-group pipeline member must still be found. It fails against the previous leader-first sequential walk and passes now. The first test still covers the leader-side case under a huge shell backlog.

Validated on Linux in WSL: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and the full cargo nextest run (3468 passed, 4 skipped) all green.

Addressed in 7b2716a8. `process_tree_pids` now gives each round-robin frontier turn a bounded slice of the shared budget (`FOREGROUND_TASK_ENTRY_PER_TURN` / `FOREGROUND_CHILD_BYTE_PER_TURN` / `FOREGROUND_CHILD_PID_PER_TURN`) and charges only what that turn consumed back to the shared totals via `ForegroundScanBudget::charge`, so unused per-turn quota stays available to later turns. A single wide expansion can no longer consume the whole probe allowance and starve the other root.

Added direct budget-accounting tests (`scan_budget_charges_only_the_consumed_share`, `scan_budget_turn_is_capped_and_spending_it_keeps_the_remainder`) and a budget-consuming callback test (`foreground_tree_traversal_reserves_enumeration_budget_per_root_turn`) that proves the shell turn still receives a slice after the leader greedily spends its own.

Validated on Linux in WSL: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, full `cargo nextest run` (3474 passed, 4 skipped), maintenance + UI hot-path contracts green.

Fixed in ff6fdd72. The per-turn task cap is removed. `process_tree_pids` now gives each root frontier its own `ForegroundScanBudget`, so the leader and the shell can no longer exhaust each other's enumeration allowance, and a single process enumerates all of its tasks up to the generous per-root limit (`FOREGROUND_TASK_ENTRY_LIMIT`, 2048) instead of stopping at 64. Heavily multithreaded agents are therefore no longer truncated at 64 threads. The 512-candidate ceiling still advances round-robin across roots.

Added `foreground_tree_traversal_reserves_enumeration_budget_per_root`, which proves the shell root keeps its own budget after the leader spends all of its own. WSL: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full nextest (3473 passed), maintenance + hot-path green.

Remaining truncation is best-effort: a process with more than 2048 threads or a child list beyond the per-root byte/pid budget is capped, which is intentional for the bounded-work guarantee.
